title: Review: Apple's hyper-pricey M5 Ultra Mac Studio made me into a vibe coder
gist: Apple's M5 Ultra Mac Studio, doubling M5 Max specs with ~1.2TB/s memory bandwidth, is positioned squarely at local LLM/agent users whose demand caught Apple off guard, but AI-driven memory shortages pushed Mac Studio prices up 25%+ (reviewed unit $12,299; 512GB model likely $20,000+). Memory capacity and bandwidth drive local AI performance, with the M5 Ultra hitting ~50 tokens/sec on Qwen 3.8 27B versus ~31 for M5 Max and 18-20 for an M2 Mac Studio.

insights.claim: Apple was caught off guard by demand for high-end Mac Studios from people running OpenClaw and open-weight models locally, which together with the AI-fueled memory shortage has made most configurations nearly impossible to buy for months.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Local AI is a new demand driver for Apple's high-margin pro desktops; supply constraints suggest unmet demand.
insights.locator: Apple was caught off guard by the demand

insights.claim: Running LLMs locally is now the core audience for the M5 Ultra Mac Studio, as Apple Silicon's unified memory, fast CPU and solid GPU fit local model and agent workloads.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple has an accidental AI hardware niche that competes with Nvidia GPUs for prosumer/developer inference.
insights.locator: That’s really the core audience for the M5 Ultra Mac Studio

insights.claim: It has become difficult to buy even a Mac mini because Apple Silicon Macs hit a sweet spot for local AI, and Apple's MLX framework has become well-optimized and supported by local-AI apps like LM Studio Bionic.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: A growing software ecosystem around MLX strengthens Apple's position in on-device AI.
insights.locator: Obviously, those top-tier systems aren’t cheap right now

insights.claim: Apple officially discontinued the Mac Pro this spring because Apple Silicon's integration of CPU, GPU and memory makes modular upgradeability superfluous or impossible.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Mac Studio is now Apple's top desktop, concentrating pro demand there.
insights.locator: This spring, Apple made it official: The Mac Pro is dead.

insights.claim: Apple raised Mac prices across the board this year because of the AI-fueled memory crunch, with the Mac Studio hit hardest given its high-end memory and storage configurations.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: AI data-center demand for memory is inflating consumer hardware prices, a tailwind for memory makers and a headwind for PC unit demand.
insights.locator: But Apple has raised prices across the board this year

insights.claim: The base M5 Max Mac Studio starts at $2,499 (up $500 from the M4 Max's $1,999), and the base M5 Ultra config costs $5,499 versus $3,999 for the equivalent M3 Ultra, a $1,500 increase.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Price hikes of 25%+ per generation quantify memory cost pass-through; watch for ASP gains vs volume effects in Apple's Mac segment.
insights.locator: At its introduction, the basic M4 Max Mac Studio ran $1,999

insights.claim: A 256GB RAM/1TB M5 Ultra Mac Studio costs $9,499 versus $5,599 for a comparable model 18 months ago, and the author expects the forthcoming 512GB version to cost $20,000 or more.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: High-capacity memory configs are where AI-driven cost inflation is steepest.
insights.locator: As for the Ultra?

insights.claim: At current prices, buying a cluster of Mac Studios for local AI feels like building a data center out of your own pocket, versus paying for Nvidia-powered cloud data centers.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Local-vs-cloud economics are shifting toward cloud as memory prices rise, limiting local AI to privacy-motivated buyers.
insights.quote: At these prices, buying a cluster of Mac Studios feels like paying to build a data center out of your own pocket.
insights.locator: As for the Ultra?

insights.claim: The author calls a fully enabled M5 Max with 64GB RAM and 1TB storage at $3,799 the price/performance sweet spot for local AI, and notes 64GB–128GB configurations cost $3,500–$5,500.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Mid-tier configs are the realistic volume sweet spot for local-AI buyers.
insights.locator: Going for a fully enabled M5 Max, 64GB of RAM

insights.claim: The M5 Ultra doubles the M5 Max's major specs, with up to 12 super cores, 24 P-cores, 80 GPU cores, 32 Neural Engine cores and about 1.2TB/s memory bandwidth, up from 819.2GB/s on the M3 Ultra.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: The bandwidth jump is the key spec for local AI inference performance.
insights.locator: The M5 Ultra is still basically a pair of M5 Max chips

insights.claim: Because the M5 Pro and M5 Max are already two chiplets joined by a silicon interconnect, the M5 Ultra is four distinct pieces of silicon packaged together, and die-to-die links can be slower than on-die communication.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple is leaning on chiplet packaging, relevant to advanced-packaging supply chains.
insights.locator: What’s different is that this generation’s M5 Pro and M5 Max

insights.claim: In testing, the M5 Ultra CPU beat the M5 Max by 80–90% and the GPU by 50–80%, and versus the M3 Ultra it was ~30% faster single-core, ~50% faster multi-core and 33–66% faster on GPU.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: A strong two-generation upgrade supports a pro refresh cycle despite higher prices.
insights.locator: In many of our general-purpose CPU and GPU tests

insights.claim: The M5 Ultra draws about 75 W in a video transcoding test, the same as the M5 Max, and was slower than the Max on H.264 encoding, suggesting it may be power-limited within the Studio's thermal envelope or affected by a bug.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Ultra chips don't scale linearly; a possible design constraint worth watching in Apple's response.
insights.locator: Looking at the power consumption numbers

insights.claim: The Mac mini's M6 very narrowly beats the M5 Ultra in single-core CPU performance, the only measure where the Ultra is not the fastest Apple Silicon chip.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple's chip cadence means newer low-end chips can edge out older flagships on single-thread.
insights.locator: General computing performance

insights.claim: For running AI models locally, GPU memory capacity and memory bandwidth matter most; bandwidth is probably the single biggest determinant of token generation speed, more than the GPU's compute.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Memory (capacity and bandwidth) is the binding constraint for AI inference hardware, reinforcing the memory-supplier thesis.
insights.locator: When you’re talking about running AI models locally

insights.claim: Coding agents need extra memory for context; context-handoff mechanisms that condense sessions lose information, so larger RAM pools materially improve local coding agent usefulness.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Agentic coding pushes demand toward higher-memory configurations.
insights.locator: On top of this, particularly for coding

insights.claim: A 64GB Apple Silicon Mac offers more GPU memory than any single consumer GPU and is far more power-efficient than an RTX 5090, even though cards like the RTX 5070 (672GB/s) exceed M5 Max bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple's unified memory is a structural advantage vs Nvidia consumer GPUs for large-model local inference.
insights.locator: Apple Silicon Macs have become popular for running these models

insights.claim: Running Qwen 3.8 27B (4K quantization) in LM Studio Bionic, the M5 Ultra generated just over 50 tokens per second versus ~31 for the M5 Max and 18–20 for an M2 Mac Studio and an AMD Strix Point-based Framework Desktop.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Hard benchmark showing bandwidth-driven inference scaling; AMD's unified-memory platform competes at the lower tier.
insights.locator: Using the 4K quantization’s default settings

insights.claim: An M5 Pro Mac mini is less usable for local coding agents even with 64GB RAM because it has half the memory bandwidth of the M5 Max.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Product segmentation by bandwidth pushes local-AI buyers up to pricier Mac Studio tiers.
insights.locator: The M5 Max Mac Studio had a tokens-per-second rate of around 31

insights.claim: The M5 generation's GPU neural accelerators dramatically reduce time to first token, making local models feel more responsive than on M4 and older chips.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Apple is tuning silicon specifically for AI inference latency.
insights.locator: On top of these stats, you also have something called “time to first token”

insights.claim: The author, who generally loathes generative AI, built a working bank-statement-PDF-to-spreadsheet web app locally with Qwen 3.8 27B, replacing a need for QuickBooks, in a couple of afternoons.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Vibe coding lets non-programmers replace niche SaaS tools, a long-term threat to small-business software subscriptions.
insights.locator: First, I had the Qwen model write a Python script

insights.claim: Data privacy is a key driver for local AI: the author could have solved the task with a few dollars of cloud tokens but would not send years of financial data to Anthropic or another provider.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Privacy concerns sustain a local-inference market that cloud AI providers cannot capture.
insights.quote: sending years of financial data to Anthropic or whoever is something I just couldn’t countenance.
insights.locator: I probably could have solved this problem in an afternoon

insights.claim: Qwen 3.8 27B is released open-weight under an Apache 2.0 license with quantizations; 32GB RAM is the practical minimum and 64GB a better target for local coding use.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Permissively licensed open-weight models make capable local coding viable on mid-tier hardware.
insights.locator: The Qwen 3.8 27B model is “open-weight”

insights.claim: The M5 Ultra Mac Studio remains a niche product for buyers with thousands of dollars who want local AI at good-but-not-cutting-edge speeds and don't want to pay OpenAI or Anthropic for tokens.
insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Local AI is a real but small segment; not a major volume driver for Apple.
insights.locator: The workloads, they are a-changing
